A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRAMA research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures, and tables support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval experiments on BEIR, MIRACL, multilingual MTEB, and MLDR, together with multiple ablation studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds NeedleRetrieval and PasskeyRetrieval results across different input lengths.

M1.justification: V2 introduces temperature scaling into the displayed InfoNCE loss, but does not explain whether this corrects the documentation or changes training. The augmentation pipeline, two-stage pruning, attention choices, and MRL procedure otherwise remain the same; expanded pruning details alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: V2 adds synthetic NeedleRetrieval and PasskeyRetrieval scenarios, extending the existing long-context evaluation beyond MLDR. Training corpora, language coverage, and the previously evaluated retrieval benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: E5-v2-base-RoPE is newly evaluated in the synthetic long-context comparisons in Tables 3, 13, and 14. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark and ablation comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds synthetic evaluations at input lengths from 256 to 32768 tokens. Section 4.3 revises the reported pruning budget from 25B total tokens to approximately 0.5B plus 26B. Table 2 also changes M3-BGE-Dense's maximum length from 512 to 8192, although Appendix Table 9 retains 512; rerunning that comparison is not established.

E4.justification: V2 adds a substantial length-sensitivity investigation using two synthetic tasks, showing degradation and model/baseline crossovers across context lengths. This directly probes extrapolation beyond the earlier aggregate MLDR evaluation. Existing ablations remain, including multilingual data balance and MRL analyses moved to Appendices A.1–A.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 13–14 add substantial new length-dependent performance profiles. For example, DRAMA0.1B scores 48.5 and 32.9 on NeedleRetrieval at 4096 and 8192 tokens. V2 also adds augmentation-cost estimates. Matched pre-existing benchmark scores and ablation results are unchanged; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds explicit mask constraints, an attention-head Lagrangian loss, and the combined pruning objective, where v1 provided a prose description referencing ShearedLlama. Section 3.1 also explicitly includes temperature in InfoNCE. These expand the mathematical specification without adding theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions present the same central contribution: diverse LLM augmentation and pruned LLM backbones enable smaller, generalizable multilingual retrievers with long-context capabilities. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion rephrase these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking synthetic long-context performance to inherited language-model context capacity. It also explains that omitting reranking augmentation can reduce generation cost roughly tenfold for a 2–3% effectiveness loss, and explicitly adds reasoning-intensive retrieval to future-work limitations.

D1.justification: V2 discloses pruned-model dimensions, attention-head counts, and layer counts in Appendix A.3, plus augmentation GPU-hour estimates. Conversely, it drops v1's explicit DRAMA release-license statement and H100 measurement footnote, and describes code/checkpoints as forthcoming. Actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting pruning, long-context evaluation, and instruction/reasoning retrieval, including Louizos et al., LongEmbed, FollowIR, and ReasonIR. It removes the MMTEB citation. The main research positioning remains; publication updates for existing references do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: V2 condenses the abstract, introduction, conclusion, and selected explanations, expands pruning exposition, and adds an ethics statement. Two existing analyses move into a reorganized Appendix A, while the overall argument and main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column report to a two-column layout. Augmentation and mixture plots are redrawn, several figures become numbered tables, and MLDR results are split into a main-text summary and an appendix table. New synthetic-result tables accompany extensive display relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: The new length sweeps directly strengthen evidence for extrapolation, while architectural specifications and cost estimates make the work easier to assess and reproduce. These useful gains are moderated by inconsistent length information in Tables 2/9 and 13/14 and reduced release-license disclosure. The main benchmark evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
